summary: We developed EcoGuide, an interactive, offline-capable web platform designed for smart agricultural adaptation in Moquegua, Peru. It is a comprehensive decision-support system that translates open NASA satellite data (POWER, GIBS, MODIS, and SMAP) and local government datasets into actionable insights through intuitive traffic-light alerts, a hydrological irrigation simulator, and a 12-month crop calendar.   The project directly addresses the Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data challenge by solving critical agricultural vulnerability in Moquegua. While traditional farming relies on intuition that fails against erratic weather, our platform empowers farmers to calculate exact weekly water needs, anticipate night frosts, and plan resilient crop rotations, achieving up to 58% in annual water savings. This is crucial because extreme climate events like El Niño and severe seasonal droughts threaten up to 40% of Moquegua's agricultural output, while river flows drop to critical levels and agriculture consumes over 80% of regional water reserves. By acting as a scientific co-pilot that respects and validates the farmer's own field experience, EcoGuide protects rural livelihoods, optimizes scarce water, and secures food production across the region.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

EcoGuide is an interactive, offline-capable web platform that translates complex NASA satellite datasets into simple, actionable agricultural decisions. By selecting a province, valley, or clicking directly on a farm plot in Moquegua, Peru, farmers and agricultural boards access four integrated modules:

  • Satellite Map (NASA GIBS & POWER): Overlays real-time vegetation health (MODIS NDVI), surface temperature, and root-zone soil moisture (SMAP) onto local farm coordinates, displaying crop stress through an intuitive traffic-light alert system.
  • Hydrological & Smart Rotation Simulator: Uses the FAO-56 Penman-Monteith methodology combined with NASA POWER meteorological data to calculate exact weekly irrigation volumes (m³/ha). It also simulates resilient crop rotations (e.g., transitioning from water-intensive Hass Avocado to frost- and drought-resilient Quinoa or Kiwicha), demonstrating up to 58% in annual water savings.
  • 12-Month Agricultural Calendar: Anticipates optimal planting windows, critical irrigation phases, and night frost risks based on local altitudinal floors.
  • Open Data & Transparency Portal: Cross-references global NASA APIs (AppEEARS, GPM IMERG, Landsat/HLS) with Peruvian government portals (MIDAGRI, SENAMHI, ANA) for parcel-level validation.

2. What benefits does it offer?

  • Extreme Water Optimization: Reduces agricultural water consumption by up to 58% through precision irrigation scheduling and climate-resilient crop rotation planning.
  • Climate Risk Mitigation: Provides early visual warnings for night frosts (< 4°C), severe droughts, and El Niño anomalies before crops suffer irreversible damage.
  • Accessibility & Offline Resilience: Brings offline support and audio diagnosis ("Listen to this section"), ensuring farmers in remote Andean valleys with intermittent connectivity or visual barriers can access critical insights.
  • Zero-Cost Decision Support: Democratizes space science using 100% open NASA and public datasets, eliminating expensive sensor hardware requirements for smallholder farmers.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

In Moquegua, climate extremes like El Niño and seasonal droughts destroy up to 40% of agricultural production, while river flows drop to critical levels (~0.6 m³/s) and agriculture consumes over 80% of regional water reserves. EcoGuide directly protects rural livelihoods and regional food security by replacing guesswork with satellite-backed precision.

Furthermore, EcoGuide is built for global scalability: because its core engine relies on global NASA satellite APIs (POWER, GIBS, MODIS, SMAP) paired with modular local agronomic profiles, our architecture can be rapidly adapted and deployed to any climate-vulnerable agricultural valley worldwide. From the Peruvian Andes to arid farming regions across Latin America, Africa, and Asia.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

  • Research & Knowledge Structuring: We used ChatGPT, Gemini and NotebookLM to synthesize, organize, and cross-reference technical documentation from NASA Earthdata resources alongside local Peruvian agronomic reports (MIDAGRI, SENAMHI, ANA) to determine the exact variables needed on the platform.
  • Development & AI-Assisted Coding: We wrote our core codebase in Visual Studio Code (VS Code) using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, leveraging AI coding assistants, specifically Codex and Google AI Studio to accelerate algorithm implementation (FAO-56 hydrological formulas), UI/UX prototyping, and API data integration.
  • Mapping & Data Visualization: Interactive geospatial rendering was built using Leaflet integrated with NASA EOSDIS GIBS tile layers, NASA POWER REST APIs, and ESRI World Imagery.
  • Deployment & Accessibility: Designed as a lightweight Progressive Web App (PWA) with Web Speech API integration for voice-assisted diagnostics and local caching for offline field usage.

5. How is your project creative?

  • Human-Centered "Co-Pilot" Philosophy: Rather than treating technology as an infallible black box that replaces traditional knowledge, EcoGuide is creatively designed as a scientific co-pilot. It respects and validates the farmer’s lifelong field intuition, presenting satellite predictions alongside low-cost and practical agronomic actions.
  • Translating Orbital Data into Human Language: Instead of overwhelming users with raw NetCDF files or complex meteorological charts, we translated multi-spectral satellite telemetry into a satelite map, intuitive color-coded traffic lights, interactive water-savings comparisons, and spoken audio summaries.
  • Scientific Honesty & Open Data Bridge: Including a dedicated "Scientific Transparency" tab that openly explains satellite resolution limits (~50 km vs. parcel scale) and links directly to national meteorological and water-authority portals bridges the gap between space agencies and local irrigation boards.
  • Farmer Feedback & Interaction: EcoGuide goes beyond providing agricultural recommendations by allowing farmers to leave questions, comments, and feedback through the "Questions & Feedback for this Section" feature. This creates a more interactive experience, encourages farmer participation, and helps connect scientific information with their real field experiences.

6. What factors did your team take into account?

  • Connectivity & Hardware Limitations: Rural farmers in high-Andean zones (1,400 to 3,100+ m.a.s.l.) often lack stable internet or high-end devices. We prioritized lightweight code, solar-friendly high-contrast UI ("Modo Sol"), and offline functionality.
  • Microclimate & Altitudinal Diversity: Moquegua spans coastal valleys (Ilo), mid-valleys (Moquegua/Samegua, Torata), and high-Andean zones (Omate, Puquina). We factored in distinct altitudinal profiles, soil types, and local flagship crops (Hass Avocado, Pisco Grapes, Oregano, Quinoa, Alfalfa).
  • Trust & Cultural Adoption: Farmers are rightfully skeptical of external tools that ignore local realities. By integrating official Peruvian data sources (SENAMHI, ANA, MIDAGRI) and framing the tool as an assistant to human judgment rather than a replacement, we ensured cultural relevance and institutional trust.
